facts.fact_text: On 15 September 2006, the applicant, acting on behalf of the unregistered organisation the Macedonian Initiative Committee, notified Blagoevgrad's mayor that the Macedonian Initiative Committee intended to stage a rally at 4 p.m. on 30 September 2006 in Macedonia Square.
The rally planned for 30 September 2006 in Macedonia Square was intended to commemorate the eighty-second anniversary of 'the day of the genocide of Macedonians in Bulgaria – 12 September 1924'.
The rally planned for 30 September 2006 in Macedonia Square would consist of the laying of wreaths and flowers and the reading of a short address.

On 28 August 2007, the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden notified the Mayor of Blagoevgrad of its intention to stage a rally on Macedonia Square, in front of Gotse Delchev's monument, at 4.30 p.m. on 12 September 2007.
The rally planned by the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden for 12 September 2007 was to mark the anniversary of 'the genocide against the Macedonians'.

The rally planned by the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden for 12 September 2007 would consist of the laying of a wreath and flowers on Gotse Delchev's monument and a short speech, and would last one hour.
On 15 September 2006, Blagoevgrad's mayor replied to the applicant that the rally planned for 30 September 2006 in Macedonia Square could not proceed.
Blagoevgrad's mayor stated that the parallel event of the concert marking the Day of Music made the staging of the rally on 30 September 2006 impossible.

In a final decision of 19 September 2006, the Blagoevgrad District Court found that Blagoevgrad's mayor's decision refusing the rally planned for 30 September 2006 was lawful, because there was a risk that the rights and freedoms of others might be infringed.
Blagoevgrad's mayor banned the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden's rally planned for 11 or 12 September 2006.

A legal challenge to Blagoevgrad's mayor's decision banning the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden's rally planned for 11 or 12 September 2006 was dismissed by the Blagoevgrad District Court on 8 September 2006.

The Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that the municipality had planned an event on Macedonia Square for 12 September 2007 — a children's holiday under the name 'Hello, school' to mark the beginning of the school year — which made the holding of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden's rally impossible.

In a final decision of 5 September 2007, the Blagoevgrad District Court dismissed the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden's application for judicial review of the ban on the rally planned for 12 September 2007.

The Blagoevgrad District Court held that the lack of registration of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden did not amount to sufficient grounds to prohibit the rally planned for 12 September 2007.

The Blagoevgrad District Court held that the fact that another event likely to draw a number of people, many of whom were children, was due to take place on the same date in Macedonia Square was enough to justify the ban on the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden's rally planned for 12 September 2007.

When a number of members and supporters of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden gathered in front of the American University in Blagoevgrad at about 5 p.m. on 12 September 2007, they were stopped by the police.
A number of members and supporters of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden were arrested by police on 12 September 2007 in Blagoevgrad.

The arrested members and supporters of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden were charged with committing administrative offences for having tried to take part in a banned rally on 12 September 2007.

On 22 October 2007, the deputy Mayor of Blagoevgrad imposed administrative punishments — fines of 200 Bulgarian levs (102.26 euros) each — on Mr Yordan Kostadinov Ivanov and on a number of members of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden for having taken part in a banned rally on 12 September 2007, in breach of a public-order regulation issued by the Blagoevgrad Municipal Council.

In a series of judgments delivered on 18 and 19 February, 11 March, and 22 and 29 May 2008, the Blagoevgrad District Court annulled the fines imposed by the deputy Mayor of Blagoevgrad on Mr Yordan Kostadinov Ivanov and members of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden.

In a decision of 30 August 2007, the Blagoevgrad Administrative Court found that under the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act, which was lex specialis in relation to the general rules of administrative procedure, the court competent to examine an application for judicial review of a Mayor's decision to ban a rally was the district court.

The Blagoevgrad District Court held that the lack of registration of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden did not amount to sufficient grounds to prohibit the rally planned for 12 September 2007.

In a final decision of 19 September 2006, the Blagoevgrad District Court found that Blagoevgrad's mayor's decision refusing the rally planned for 30 September 2006 was lawful, because there was a risk that the rights and freedoms of others might be infringed.
The Blagoevgrad District Court noted that Bulgarian society was particularly sensitive to assertions that a Macedonian minority existed in Bulgaria and that its rights were being infringed.

The Blagoevgrad District Court held that the fact that another event likely to draw a number of people, many of whom were children, was due to take place on the same date in Macedonia Square was enough to justify the ban on the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden's rally planned for 12 September 2007.
